subjects.full_text: 1.0 INTRODUCTION This Physics format for the Form Two National Assessment is based on the Physics Syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education 2024, issued by the Tanzania Institute of Education (TIE). This Format focuses on the competences acquired by students at Form One and Two levels. The format emphasises a comprehensive evaluation of higher-order thinking skills, practical skills, as highlighted in the current syllabus. 2.0 MAIN COMPETENCES The assessment will test the students’ ability to apply knowledge of Physics in various contexts. 3.0 ASSESSMENT RUBRIC The Physics assessment will comprise one (1) theory paper with a duration of 2:30 hours. For students with special needs, the duration of the assessment will be 2:55 hours. The paper will consist of sections A, B and C, with a total of ten (10) questions. Students will be required to answer all the questions in each section. The paper will carry 100 marks. Section A will have two (2) objective questions. Question 1 will include ten (10) multiple-choice items, each carrying one (1) mark, making a total of 10 marks. Question 2 will be a matching items question, consisting of five (5) items, each carrying one (1) mark, making a total of five (5) marks. Therefore, the section will weigh a total of 15 marks. Section B will have seven (7) short answer questions, each carrying 10 marks, making a total of seventy (70) marks. Section C will have one (1) structured/essay question carrying 15 marks. Note: When responding to questions, students will be allowed to use non-programmable calculators. 48 4.0 COMPETENCES TO BE ASSESSED The students will be assessed in applying knowledge of Physics in various contexts, specifically student ability to: 4.1 demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles of Physics; 4.2 demonstrate mastery of basic terminologies, measurements and symbols in Physics; and 4.3 use mathematics to explain physical principles and phenomena. 5.0 TABLE OF SPECIFICATION FOR 031 PHYSICS Skills to be Tested g n s y i l a n A g n i t a u a v E l g n i t a e r C i g n y p p A l S/N Main Competence Specific Competences g n i r e b m e m e R i g n d n a t s r e d n U 1. subjects.introduction: This Form Two National Assessment Format for Mathematics has been prepared in accordance with the Mathematics Syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education issued by the Tanzania Institute of Education in 2023. Basically, the format describes the skills to be the percentage weight per tested, competence(s) and specific competences outlined in the Mathematics Syllabus. It aims to serve as a guideline for assessors to evaluate the mathematical competences and skills acquired by students during their two years of secondary education. the number of items,
subjects.general_objectives: The assessment will test the students’ ability to demonstrate mastery of: 2.1 mathematical language; 2.2 basic concepts in geometry and algebra; and 2.3 basic concepts in coordinate geometry, trigonometry, circles, vectors, probability and statistics.
subjects.general_competences: The Mathematics assessment will comprise one (1) paper lasting for 2:30 hours. For students with special needs, the duration of the assessment will be 3:20 hours. The paper will consist of 10 questions. The student will be required to answer all the questions. Each question will carry 10 marks, making a total of 100 marks for the whole paper. Note: Students will be allowed to use non-programmable calculators.
subjects.rubric: Students will be assessed in the following competences: 4.1 Demonstrating mastery of mathematical language. 4.1.1 using numerical skills in different contexts; 62 4.1.2 using ratios and proportions in daily life; and 4.1.3 using rates and variations in different contexts. 4.2 Demonstrating mastery of basic concepts in geometry and algebra. 4.2.1 using geometry, approximations, functions in various contexts; relations, and 4.2.2 using algebra and matrices in problem solving; and 4.2.3 using sets, sequences and series in problem solving. 4.3 Demonstrating mastery of basic concepts in coordinate trigonometry, circles, vectors, probability and geometry, statistics. 4.3.1 using basic coordinate geometry, trigonometry, and vectors skills in daily life.
